A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Performative Validity of Recourse Explanations. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renamed experimental settings.

before.justification: Section 6, Figure 3, and Appendix F report original simulations across five synthetic causal models and a data-fitted college-admission setting.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional Credit experiments and original/refitted classifier accuracies reported in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The causal action model, CE/CR/ICR objectives, individualized and subpopulation estimators, and evolutionary optimization procedure are retained. The random-forest addition supplies the new Credit simulation setting.

E1.justification: V2 adds a data-fitted credit-scoring setting with eleven features, extending coverage beyond the two-feature settings in v1. The five synthetic settings and GPA experiment remain; shortened synthetic-setting names do not represent new datasets.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate CE, individualized CR, subpopulation CR, individualized ICR, and subpopulation ICR. V2 applies this same comparator set to Credit without adding or removing methods in the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: The added Credit experiment uses a nonlinear random-forest SCM with Gaussian noise. Table 2 introduces classification-accuracy evaluation of original and refitted models on both original and post-recourse test data. Existing experiments retain their stated training sizes, recourse sample counts, splits, and refitting mixture.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a diagnostic analysis of how predictive accuracy changes under recourse and refitting, comparing both classifiers across both data distributions. This supplements the existing acceptance-rate analysis; no new method ablations or sensitivity sweeps are introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten runs with seeds 40–49 and retain Table 1 standard deviations and Figure 3's range/error-bar conventions. The new accuracy table averages ten runs without introducing a new uncertainty estimator, significance test, or increased run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Credit acceptance-rate differences of -0.47 for CE, -0.49/-0.39 for individualized/subpopulation CR, and +0.01 for both ICR variants. For CE on LinAdd/LAdd, the expected distribution difference changes from -0.70 ± 0.14 to -0.71 ± 0.13, the minimum from -0.96 to -0.97, and acceptance difference from -0.94 to -0.95. Other matched Table 1 entries are unchanged. Table 2 adds classifier-accuracy results.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.1 and Appendix C distinguish equality with the post-recourse predictor h^p from equality with the mixture predictor h^m. The proof's final implication also corrects the acceptance-region condition from predicted label 0 to 1. Appendix E.1 adds an explicit mixture-predictor inequality; the principal assumptions and theorems remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: recourse can invalidate itself through dependence on or interventions upon effect variables, and the analysis favors improvement-focused recourse under the stated assumptions. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 2 reverses v1's characterization of gaming and improvement: v2 attributes marginal-only shifts to improvement and possible conditional shifts to gaming, then explains the additional role of individual-dependent information leakage. Appendix F.3 newly explains that accuracy can decline despite continued model optimality because recourse moves observations closer to the decision boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds Credit construction details: fitting random forests from causal parents and Gaussian distributions to residuals. Section 6 and Appendix F.1 inconsistently reverse the data and causal-graph source attributions. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, timing disclosures, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 condenses the performative-prediction and strategic-classification literature, removing citations including Izzo et al. and Bechavod et al. V2 adds Pfister et al. (2021) and the Yeh dataset reference, and more explicitly positions individual-dependent information leakage relative to prior gaming/improvement analyses. The overarching research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites portions of the introductory example and Section 4, condenses related work, and expands explanations in Appendices D.1 and E.1. It also adds the NeurIPS checklist and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference formatting throughout, turns Figure 1 into a text-wrapped inset, and substantially redraws Figure 2 with coordinated panels, node styling, and colors. Figure 3 and Table 1 gain Credit entries, and a new Table 2 displays classifier accuracies. These constitute broad visual and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: The added eleven-feature Credit experiment broadens evidence beyond v1's two-feature settings. Accuracy diagnostics, targeted proof corrections, and clearer causal diagrams also help readers assess the argument. These are bounded gains because the central findings remain largely unchanged, while inconsistent Credit source attributions between Section 6 and Appendix F.1 weaken reproducibility of the added experiment.
